# v0.49.63

This patch fixes OpenCode 2 sessions that run with Magic Context's compaction off: OpenCode's own automatic compaction no longer repeats on every step. It also stops the record of a `/ctx-flush` decision from being lost now and then.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode or Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: native compaction repeated on every step with Magic Context's compaction off (issue 944, thanks @endynamoo for the report and the diagnosis in pull request 945):** with `compaction.enabled: false`, Magic Context leaves context management to the host. But on OpenCode 2 it still put back the history that sat before OpenCode's own compaction checkpoint. The request never shrank, so OpenCode compacted again on the next step, and again after that. With compaction off, Magic Context now sends OpenCode's checkpoint and the messages after it exactly as OpenCode built them. When one of its passes fails in that mode, it sends OpenCode's own request instead of refusing the turn, because the refusal only protected the restore. With compaction on, nothing changes.
- **The record of a `/ctx-flush` decision was sometimes lost:** each pass's decision is written to Magic Context's store a moment after the pass. On Pi and Oh My Pi that write was dropped whenever the next run ended first. On OpenCode it gave up at once when another connection, such as the host's own message indexing, held the store's lock. The write now survives a finished run, and on OpenCode it retries for about two seconds without blocking the host. The flush itself always happened and requests are unchanged; only the record, which diagnostics and the cache analyzer read, was missing.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.21.0
releases.body:
## Magic Context Dashboard 0.21.0

### New

- **Workspace menu on project cards.** Right-click a project card, or press the Menu key or Shift+F10 on a focused card, to add the project to a workspace or move it to another one. Workspaces that already hold a project with the same name, the project's current workspace, and home-directory projects are shown disabled, with the reason. Changing membership never changes a workspace's sharing settings. Thanks to @yiyi-wei (#912).
- **A stable token in serve mode.** `--serve` keeps its access token in a file, so a browser tab or script keeps working across restarts. Thanks to @yiyi-wei (#897).
- **`embedding.dimensions`.** The config editor accepts an output width for OpenAI-compatible embedding providers that support it, such as Qwen3-Embedding at 768, 1024 or 4096. Test Connection fails with a clear message when the width is invalid (#405).

### Fixed

- Dismissing a user memory that was already dismissed no longer changes its timestamp or refreshes the profile again (#900).
- The cache view names a pass that removed the latest turn's thinking after a provider refused it, instead of showing it as unexplained.
- Updated dashboard dependencies with security fixes.

# v0.49.62

This patch stops Pi from rewriting earlier replies on every tool turn when the model's provider adds an empty text block after a tool call. The rewrites cost most of the prompt cache on each turn.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi: prompt cache lost on almost every tool turn with Gemini (issue 948, thanks @enterlet for the report and the root-cause analysis):** some providers, Gemini through `pi-antigravity` among them, end a reply that calls a tool with an empty text block. Magic Context gives no tag to an empty block, but its check for edited replies still counted the block, so it judged the reply edited on the next turn. It then gave the reply a new tag number and rewrote it in the request. That changed bytes the provider had already cached, so most of the conversation was sent uncached again, and cache hits fell from about 90% to 15–30%. The check now skips exactly the blocks that get no tag, so the request only grows at the end. A reply whose text really changed still gets a new number, as before. Replies already renumbered keep their current number. Oh My Pi drops the empty block itself, and OpenCode has no such check, so neither was affected.

# v0.49.61

This patch makes Oh My Pi advisors work with Magic Context again on Oh My Pi 18.20.2 and later.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi: every advisor turn refused, then the advisor halted (issue 940, thanks @Qiiks for the report):** Magic Context lets an Oh My Pi advisor's own requests through its safety check by recognising OMP's stock advisor prompt. Oh My Pi 18.20.2 removed the block that prompt used to start with, so on 18.20.2 and later no advisor was recognised, stock or customised, and each advisor turn was refused until OMP stopped the advisor. Magic Context now recognises the stock advisor prompt with or without that block. Your own `instructions:` in `WATCHDOG.yml` still work, because Oh My Pi adds them after the stock prompt. An advisor request after Oh My Pi compacts the advisor's own context is now recognised too; before, it was refused on every version. Main-session requests are checked exactly as before: a prompt you type that starts like an advisor update is still not treated as one.

# v0.49.60

This patch fixes Pi sessions that could stop shrinking after Pi's own compaction or a failed reply, makes Magic Context take over when Pi reports a context overflow, counts images at their token cost instead of their size in bytes, and fixes Oh My Pi's `antigravity-cli` provider re-compacting after every compaction.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart the host. No database migration is needed.

A Pi or Oh My Pi session whose newest history summary ends partway through a turn rebuilds its request once after the update. That turn's prompt comes back, so the model sees the prompt it is answering. Sessions whose summary ends at the end of a turn send exactly the same requests as before.

## Fixed

- **Pi: a session stopped shrinking and kept sending its summarized history (issue 938, thanks @expiren for the detailed report and the session details):** Magic Context removes the messages a history summary covers by finding the summary's last message in the request. When Pi hides that message (a failed reply it retries), Magic Context places the cut by position in the session instead. That fallback gave up whenever the request also held Pi's own compaction summary, so every summarized message, images included, stayed in the request on every turn. The fallback now cuts exactly as the normal path does, and logs when a cut cannot be placed instead of silently cutting nothing. It never removes the prompt of the turn the summary ends in, so the model never answers a prompt it can't see.
- **Pi: a request could go out without the history summary:** if inserting the summary failed, the turn went out with neither the summary nor the cut. Magic Context now replays the last good request, or refuses the turn when there is none.
- **Pi: overflows that Pi detected left Magic Context's recovery off (issue 938):** Pi recognises some provider errors as context overflows that Magic Context's own patterns missed. Magic Context now also asks the running host's overflow check, and it arms its overflow recovery when Pi is about to retry a request that failed for an overflow. A reply that succeeded but reported more input than Pi's configured window arms nothing, because the provider accepted it.
- **Pi: images counted at their size in bytes (issue 938):** a base64 image counted as tens of thousands of tokens in Magic Context's size checks, and images in tool outputs counted as fixed, so the emergency drop could not remove them. Images now count at a fixed token cost per image, can be dropped with the tool output that carries them, and no longer block replaying the last good request.
- **Oh My Pi, `antigravity-cli`: compacting again right after a compaction (issue 939, thanks @DeemoASCII):** this provider reports each tool-call step with only `usage.contextTokens`. Magic Context ignored that field, so after a compaction it kept reading the old peak and compacted again. It now uses `contextTokens` when the other usage counters are all zero; other providers are unchanged. `antigravity-cli` also gets the same window as `google-antigravity`, whose output is not reserved out of the input window.
